outlook: Grains slid to multi-month lows Tuesday on bigger global supply prospects and U.S. harvest pressure: November soybeans fell 12 cents to $12.29¼, December corn lost 6¼ cents to $4.48¾, Chicago December wheat dropped 5¾ cents to $6.10¼, and Minneapolis December spring wheat fell 5½ cents to $6.28½. Higher-than-USDA crop estimates for Australian and Argentine wheat and Argentine corn added pressure, and the weaker Brazilian real after Brazil's election keeps U.S. soybeans pricier for export buyers. Corn, soybeans and Chicago wheat bounced 1–2½ cents overnight, while spring wheat stayed slightly lower and ICE canola gained about C$2.70. Traders are watching the Fed rate decision at 1 pm CT today and November soybean first notice day on Friday.
